deep.reconstruction:
Setting. F(s,z)=0 is an irreducible algebraic curve of genus p, and T is its Riemann surface cut along 2p cross-cuts. The phi_pi(s,z), pi=1..p, are the adjoint polynomials of the p everywhere-finite integrals. Hence omega_pi = phi_pi dz/(dF/ds) is a basis of the holomorphic differentials. The page belongs to Riemann's integration of the Abel differential equations by means of p+1 moving points (Jacobi inversion). The neighbouring sheet, transcribed as the 'next' page but logically preceding this one, sets this up. It writes the p+1 points as functions of a parameter theta, where 1/theta is a rational function with simple poles at the p+1 initial points. 1/theta is built from sum beta_nu t(s_nu^0,z_nu^0) + sum alpha_nu w_nu + const with all periods made 0. It then turns to the degenerate case where only m of the beta are nonzero and p+1-m vanish.

(A) Degenerate case, end of the argument.
(1) When m of the beta are nonzero, 1/theta has poles only at the first m initial points. Its m-valued inverse gives m moving points (s_1,z_1)..(s_m,z_m) satisfying, for pi=1..p:
    sum_{nu=1}^{m} phi_pi(s_nu,z_nu) dz_nu/(dF/ds)(s_nu,z_nu) = 0.
    This is Abel's theorem applied to the fibres of the function theta.
(2) Regard this as p linear homogeneous equations in the m unknowns X_nu = dz_nu/(dF/ds)(s_nu,z_nu). Riemann states that p-m of them (as transcribed; see errors) are consequences of the others.
(3) The full system has p equations in the p+1 unknowns X_1..X_{p+1}, and for distinct generic points it fixes their ratios completely. This system is satisfied by taking X_1..X_m equal to the solution of the reduced system and X_{m+1}=...=X_{p+1}=0.
(4) Hence dz_nu = 0 for nu>m. The points (s_{m+1},z_{m+1})..(s_{p+1},z_{p+1}) are constant and keep their initial values. A first attempt, saying these points are 'unbestimmt', is crossed out and replaced by: they keep their initial values.
    Modern reading: if the initial divisor D of degree p+1 contains a subdivisor D_m with l(D_m)=2, the motion takes place in the pencil |D_m|. The rest of D stays fixed. By Riemann-Roch, i(D_m) = p-m+1, so the m x p evaluation matrix has rank m-1.

(B) Abelian integrals and periods.
- Put w_pi = integral of phi_pi(s,z) dz/(dF/ds) + const, integrated through the interior of T, so w_pi is single-valued on T.
- Let k_pi^nu be the periodicity modulus of w_pi across the nu-th cross-cut, nu=1..2p.
- So when (s,z) passes from the negative to the positive side of cut nu, (w_1..w_p) changes simultaneously by the period vector (k_1^nu..k_p^nu).

(C) Congruence modulo the period lattice.
- Definition: (b_1..b_p) is congruent to (a_1..a_p) with respect to the 2p systems of associated moduli, written (b) ≡ (a), iff b_pi = a_pi + sum_{nu=1}^{2p} m_nu k_pi^nu for pi=1..p, with integers m_nu. In modern terms, b-a lies in the lattice Lambda in C^p.
- Claim: any p complex numbers can be written in one and only one way as a_pi = sum_nu xi_nu k_pi^nu with 2p real xi_nu. Equivalently, the 2p period vectors are R-linearly independent and span C^p = R^{2p}. This rests on the positivity / bilinear relations (Riemann 1857).
- Consequence: let each xi_nu run over a half-open interval [c, c+1). This picks exactly one representative from each congruence class, i.e. a fundamental parallelotope of C^p/Lambda, the Jacobian.

The wording closely matches the published 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (J. reine angew. Math. 54, 1857), second part. The sheet appears to be a draft of it.
errors: Counting in (A)(2): for the m moving points the reduced system has rank m-1 (i(D_m) = p-m+1 by Riemann-Roch). So p-m+1 of the p equations are consequences of the others, not p-m. Otherwise the m unknowns would be forced to vanish. Example: genus 2, m=2, points (x,y),(x,-y): both equations reduce to the same trivial relation, so p-m+1=1 is dependent, whereas p-m=0. Either Riemann slipped by one, or the manuscript reads 'p+1-m' (the image near the start of that line is partly struck and ambiguous).

The claim that the p+1 quantities have their ratios 'völlig bestimmt' holds only for general position (rank p of the (p+1) x p matrix). This is not justified on the page, though it is the natural generic assumption.

The unique real decomposition a_pi = sum xi_nu k_pi^nu needs the R-linear independence of the 2p period vectors. That is asserted without proof here; it follows from Riemann's bilinear inequality, proved elsewhere.

results.what: Degenerate case of the integration of Abel's differential equations: if only m of the p+1 points move (poles of theta at m points), the remaining p+1-m stay fixed at their initial values.
results.modern_name: Special divisors / linear pencils in the Jacobi inversion problem (Riemann-Roch, index of speciality)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (Abelian functions); Clebsch-Gordan, Brill-Noether for special divisors

results.what: Normal integrals w_pi on the cut surface T and their periodicity moduli k_pi^nu across the 2p cross-cuts
results.modern_name: Period matrix of a compact Riemann surface

results.what: Congruence of p-tuples modulo the 2p simultaneous period systems
results.modern_name: Period lattice Lambda in C^p; Jacobian variety C^p/Lambda
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (four-fold periodicity, 1834-35); Riemann 1857 for the general notation

results.what: Unique real coordinates xi_nu with respect to the 2p period vectors; a unit cube in xi gives exactly one representative per class
results.modern_name: Fundamental domain of a lattice in R^{2p}; R-independence of periods

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material that appears almost verbatim in Riemann's published 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen': the congruence notation, the period moduli, and the Abel differential equations with the degenerate case. It is of interest only as drafting evidence; it contains one probable off-by-one slip.

checkable.asserts: Genus-2 example y^2=f(x), points (x,y),(x,-y) moving together: the first Abel equation sum dz/(dF/ds) holds (equals 0).
The second equation also holds (equals 0). Both equations collapse to one relation, so the rank is m-1=1 and p-m+1=1 equation is dependent.
Riemann-Roch: with l(D)=2 and deg D=m, i(D)=l(D)-deg D-1+p = p-m+1, the number of dependent equations.
For genus 1 with periods 1 and tau=r+I*t (t>0), the real 2x2 matrix [[1,r],[0,t]] has determinant t ≠ 0. So every complex a = xi1*1 + xi2*tau has unique real xi.
Explicit unique real decomposition of a=0.3+0.7i with respect to periods 1 and tau=1/2+3i/2.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: the count before '-m' is ambiguous in the image ('p-m' vs 'p+1-m', with partial strike-through). Mathematically it should be p+1-m.
'k_pi^nu' is written as capital-looking K_pi^nu in the manuscript.
'durch das Innere von T integrirt' replaces the struck 'genommen'; '+const' is inserted above the integral.

'congruent' is written above a struck word; the final lines read roughly 'erhält man aus jeder Reihe congruenter Systeme ein und nur eines, wenn man jede Grösse xi alle Werthe von einem beliebigen Werthe bis zu einem um 1 grösseren Werthe ... durchlaufen lässt'.
The congruence definition is drafted twice: first 'Ein System ... congruent ... genannt werden', then 'so schreiben wir (b_1..b_p) ≡ (a_1..a_p), wenn b_pi = a_pi + sum m_nu k_pi^nu'.
